design.text: Multi-center, open-label, randomized controlled trial using an investigational active control (ZMapp), with a superiority design; all subjects received optimized standard of care.

citations.quote: The efficacy of INMAZEB was evaluated in PALM, a multi-center, open-label, randomized controlled trial sponsored by the National Institute of Allergy and Infectious Diseases (NIAID; NCT03719586).
The PALM trial compared three investigational agents (two mAb products and one small molecule) to an investigational control ZMapp (another mAb).

population.text: Subjects of all ages, including pregnant women, with documented Zaire ebolavirus infection and symptoms of any duration, receiving optimized standard of care.

The primary efficacy endpoint was 28-day mortality.

n.text: Primary (ITT concurrent) population: INMAZEB N=154, Control N=153.

citations.quote: efficacy endpoint, reduction in 28-day mortality, in the REGN-EB3 arm compared to ZMapp. Mortality in subjects concurrently enrolled in the intention-to-treat (ITT) population was 52/154 (33.8%) in the REGN-EB3 arm and 78/153 (51.0%) in the ZMapp arm with a rate difference of -17.2% (95% confidence interval -28.0% to -4.1%).

result.text: 28-day mortality 52/154 (34%) with INMAZEB vs 78/153 (51%) control; mortality rate difference -17.2% (95% CI -28.4, -2.6); p=0.0024.

indication.text: Indicated for the treatment of infection caused by Zaire ebolavirus in adult and pediatric patients, including neonates born to a mother who is RT-PCR positive for Zaire ebolavirus infection.

citations.quote: INMAZEB is indicated for the treatment of infection caused by *Zaire ebolavirus* in adult and pediatric patients, including neonates born to a mother who is RT-PCR positive for *Zaire ebolavirus* infection [see *Dosage and Administration (2.2)*, and *Clinical Studies (14)*].

target_moa.text: Combination of three recombinant human IgG1κ monoclonal antibodies each targeting the Zaire ebolavirus glycoprotein (GP); maftivimab neutralizes and blocks viral entry, odesivimab is non-neutralizing and induces FcγRIIIa effector function and also binds secreted GP (sGP), and atoltivimab combines neutralization and FcγRIIIa signaling activities.

citations.quote: INMAZEB is a combination of three recombinant human IgG1κ monoclonal antibodies each targeting the *Zaire ebolavirus* glycoprotein (GP).

Maftivimab is a neutralizing antibody that blocks entry of the virus into susceptible cells. Odesivimab is a non-neutralizing antibody that induces antibody-dependent effector function through Fc\gammaRIIIa signaling when bound to its target. Odesivimab also binds to the soluble form of *Zaire ebolavirus* glycoprotein (sGP). Atoltivimab combines both neutralization and Fc\gammaRIIIa signaling activities.

modality.text: mAb (combination of three human IgG1κ monoclonal antibodies)

citations.quote: INMAZEB is an antiviral drug combination of three recombinant human IgG1κ monoclonal antibodies (atoltivimab, maftivimab, and odesivimab) that inhibit *Zaire ebolavirus* [see *Microbiology (12.4)*].

key_safety.text: Most common adverse events (≥20% of INMAZEB subjects) were pyrexia, chills, tachycardia, tachypnea, and vomiting. Table 3 rates (INMAZEB vs control): pyrexia 54% vs 58%, chills 39% vs 33%, tachycardia 20% vs 32%, tachypnea 19% vs 28%, vomiting 19% vs 23%, hypotension 15% vs 31%. Infusion-related reactions including anaphylaxis are potential safety concerns.

requirement.text: 3936-1: Conduct a phenotypic study to determine impact on binding and antiviral activity against REGN-EB3 and the individual mAbs using pseudotyped particles containing GP substitutions I274M, W275L, G528R, I544T, H549R, N563T, and E564A.

citations.quote: 3936-1 Conduct a phenotypic study to determine the impact on binding and antiviral activity against REGN-EB3, atoltivimab (REGN3470), odesivimab (REGN3471), and maftivimab (REGN3479) using lentivirus-based particles pseudotyped with *Zaire ebolavirus* (EBOV) glycoprotein (GP) containing these substitutions to determine shifts in susceptibility: I274M, W275L, G528R, I544T, H549R, N563T, and E564A.

requirement.text: 3936-2: Characterize genotypically/phenotypically known resistant variants of the individual mAbs and those from VSV-based chimeric virus escape studies, and assess cross-resistance between atoltivimab and odesivimab resistant variants using an ADCC assay.

citations.quote: 3936-2 Conduct a study to characterize genotypically/phenotypically known atoltivimab (REGN3470), odesivimab (REGN3471), and maftivimab (REGN3479) resistant variants and those identified through VSV-based chimeric virus cell culture escape studies with respect to binding, neutralization, and ADCC assays with the individual mAbs (REGN3470, REGN3471, REGN3479) and the REGN-EB3 mAb combination (INMAZEB). Specifically assess cross-resistance between atoltivimab (REGN3470) and odesivimab (REGN3471) resistant variants using an ADCC assay.

requirement.text: 3936-3: Submit a final report with complete, unblinded safety data for all subjects treated with REGN-EB3 during the PALM Extension Phase.

citations.quote: 3936-3 Submit a final report with complete, unblinded safety data for all subjects who were enrolled after interim results of the initial phase of the PALM trial and were treated with atoltivimab, maftivimab, and odesivimab-ebgn (REGN-EB3) for *Zaire ebolavirus* infection during the PALM Extension Phase.

requirement.text: 3936-5: Perform complete resistance analysis of sequences derived from subjects treated with REGN-EB3 in the PALM trial, if access to the data becomes available.

citations.quote: 3936-5 Perform complete resistance analysis of sequences derived from subjects treated with REGN-EB3 in the PALM trial, if access to the data becomes available.

requirement.text: 3936-6: Design and conduct a trial evaluating a higher dose of INMAZEB vs INMAZEB 150 mg/kg in Zaire ebolavirus-infected patients with CtNP values ≤22 to determine if a change in dosing regimen is needed.

citations.quote: 3936-6 Collaborate with US public health agencies, other public health agencies, and local health authorities, as appropriate to design and conduct a trial to evaluate the efficacy, safety and pharmacokinetics of a higher dose of INMAZEB (atoltivimab, maftivimab, and odesivimab-ebgn) vs. INMAZEB 150 mg/kg in *Zaire ebolavirus*-infected adult and pediatric patients with cycle threshold (CT) values for nucleoprotein targets of less than or equal to 22 to determine if a change in dosing regimen is needed in these patients.

summary.text: INMAZEB received Orphan Drug designation (2016) and Breakthrough Therapy designation (2019) for EBOV infection, was granted rolling review (October 2019) and Priority Review, and was approved on the basis of the PALM trial demonstrating superiority in reducing 28-day mortality; no advisory committee was convened.

citations.quote: The regulatory history is notable for Orphan Drug designation and Breakthrough Therapy designation. This BLA received a Priority Review and was not presented at the Antimicrobial Drugs Advisory Committee because REGN-EB3 received Breakthrough Designation and the benefit-risk assessment was not controversial based on the review team's preliminary assessment of the trial results.
- Orphan Drug designation (#16-5363) for REGN-EB3 for the treatment of patients with EBOV infection was granted on July 14, 2016.
- Breakthrough Therapy designation for REGN-EB3 for the treatment of EBOV infection was granted on September 3, 2019.
- Rolling review was granted on October 2, 2019.

The Applicant's primary efficacy results were confirmed by the statistical review team and demonstrated superiority of REGN-EB3 compared to ZMapp in reducing the 28-day mortality rate in subjects with confirmed EVD (Table 12).
